title: Lekalo PHP Operations Input
description: Closed independent contract for the bounded PHP Laravel use-case generation input (issue #59). The document is authored under `lekalo/operations/`, names the exact compiled-IR evidence digest it consumes and the exact types-input digest whose type surface the handlers reuse, and declares one bounded record per generated or checked operation. The compiled IR is never embedded: the adapter reads the core-staged evidence named by projectId from the canonical cache home and refuses any digest divergence. Supported recipes are a closed subset; anything else refuses before any write. The document is pure data - no credentials, hosts, URLs, users, wall-clock timestamps, or provider output.

projectId.description: The project id whose compiled IR evidence is consumed; the same id the core stages at `.lekalo/cache/ir/<projectId>.json`.

irDigest.description: The exact digest of the consumed IR evidence bytes; any divergence between this digest and the staged evidence is a binding refusal, never a best-effort read.

typesInputDigest.description: The exact digest of the `lekalo/types/<projectId>.types.json` document whose mapped type surface the operation handlers reuse. The types family is a required dependency: a missing or diverging types input refuses the whole operations join.

policy.description: The closed operations policy. Absent members take their documented defaults; unknown members refuse. v0.4.0 has no custody member: custody is per operation record, and the scaffold root is the closed shared constant `app/lekalo-operations`, never a configurable path.

operations.description: One record per operation. The array is canonical: sorted by id, duplicates refuse.

semanticId.description: A module-qualified lowercase Lekalo symbol id (`module.name`).

namespacePrefix.description: The generated PHP namespace prefix. The semantic module becomes one additional namespace segment, so the full FQN is `<prefix>\<Module>\<Class>`.

id.description: The semantic id of an IR command or query definition; the kinds must agree.

mode.description: managed: generated regenerable handler from a declared recipe. scaffold-once: one emission of the signature under the closed consumer root, then maintained. checked: no writes; the declared shape joins against the observed evidence. custom: maintained body with the same shape join and no business-body rewriting.

entry.description: Required for checked and custom: the declared native entrypoint the observed evidence must join.

recipe.description: Required for managed; the closed managed recipe. Any member beyond the closed grammar refuses.

errors.description: The declared typed failures of the operation. Must equal (as a sorted set) the #62 error-registry binding of this operation id; infrastructure-category members of that binding stay infrastructure and never become domain classes.

policy.description: The declared authorization binding: an IR policy definition whose `applies_to` names this operation. Absence is a declared fact (the operation has no policy port), never an implicit public.

transaction.description: The declared transaction binding (commands only). Absent means forbidden: a query or an unbound command never opens a transaction, and absence is never read as ambient defaults.

mode.description: required: the wrapper runs the body inside one TransactionPort run. forbidden: the body must not open one. v0.4.0 has no optional mode - an isolation-optional declaration refuses as unsupported.

fqn.description: The case-preserving native PHP FQN of the entrypoint class.

method.description: The single public business entrypoint method name. v0.4.0 closes it to `handle`.

path.description: The lowercase logical source path of the maintained class.

port.description: The injected port interface name stem (PascalCase, without module segment). The emitter declares one interface with one method; the maintained implementation carries the actual body.

result.description: Commands may declare a typed result ref (an IR definition id). Queries derive their result from the IR `returns`; declaring one here is redundant and refuses.

entity.description: The updated entity definition id (IR kind `entity`).

key.description: The input field carrying the entity identity value; its type must equal the entity's identity field type.

assignments.description: The explicit field assignments. Every assigned operand must type-match the entity field; one assignment per field, duplicates refuse.

kept.description: The entity fields carried over unchanged. Every entity field is either assigned exactly once or kept exactly once - partial coverage refuses.

preconditions.description: Typed equality preconditions checked after the read and before the write; a failed precondition throws one declared error.

missingBehavior.description: The bounded missing-record behavior. v0.4.0 supports exactly one: throw one declared error.

emit.description: Declared event emissions after the successful save. Every event payload field must be covered exactly once by a typed operand; the event id must be emitted by an IR effect named by the command.

operand.description: One closed typed operand: an input field value, the read entity's field value, one enum case of the target type, or a scalar literal. No expressions, no clock, no ID generation, no callbacks.

value.description: The declared enum value, verbatim as the IR declares it.
